items.title: Gus Fontenet Interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER: A Coyson music? INTERVIEWEE: It wasn't Coyson, it was all brass on.

ctx.x: Mr. Fontenet, would you tell us something about your music training when you were a child, something about your music in your home and so on? Well, music training when I was a child, in my home, I started learning music when I was 17 years old. And as I said, with Vanna Band, Adam Broussard, Herbert McPuldoon and I, we were the farmers. We got a Vanna Band and then Tom Edwards, we got Tom Edwards, Robert Stafford, Pete Broussard, Peter Broussard, that's a brother, Adam. Where did your group meet, Mr. Fontenet, at…

Almost every night of the week or just the weekend? At that time we were playing every night. Oh my. I guess people really like to dance a lot more than they do now. After they start to be nightclubs, the dances start to fall off. Well that's a surprising statement to make, isn't it? I wonder why. Generally speaking, were the people who attended the dances at this time pretty well behaved Mr. Fontenet? Most of them were. You didn't have to have a floor walk in those?
